div.div:
Attack traffic travels from the Palo Alto Networks cloud to your
target, not from the machine you are sitting at. Nothing here can
prove that path.
Confirm the target separately by calling it the way an ordinary
client would, from outside your network if it is meant to be public.
If it is private, the Network Channel or an allowlisted source IP is
what carries the traffic, and check 5 covers the first of those.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 664px; height: 1px; padding-top: 717px; margin-left: 717px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #00294D; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: Run check 5 from inside the cluster, not near it

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 648px; height: 1px; padding-top: 737px; margin-left: 719px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
kubectl run curl-test --image=curlimages/curl --rm -it
--restart=Never -- curl -v https://registry.ai-red-teaming.
paloaltonetworks.com/
A NetworkPolicy on the namespace is invisible from the node, from
a bastion, and from your laptop. The only honest test is a pod on
the same namespace the channel client will run in.
